title: The ear of the ear
hookLine: the teacher answers: behind every sense is the self, the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind
carry: the atman is the ear of the ear
tomorrow: The eye does not go there

cards: In a dark movie theater, a whole film goes by, the car chase, the kiss, the explosion, and nobody in the seats looks at the light. But without the projector's beam, there's nothing on the screen at all.
Every image is made of it, and it's the one thing nobody watches. Yesterday the student asked who moves the mind. Today the teacher answers, and his answer sounds like a riddle.
It's really a description of that light.

teach.b: Verse two. It is the ear of the ear.
The mind of the mind. The speech of speech. The breath of breath.
The eye of the eye. Shrotrasya shrotram: the hearing of hearing. What does that mean?
Your ear hears sounds, but something is aware of the hearing itself: something knows that you are hearing. That's the ear of the ear. Your mind thinks thoughts; something is aware of the thinking.
That's the mind of the mind. The Kena points past each sense to the awareness it runs on, the way you'd point past the picture to the light.
Hindu teachers have a name for that listener in you: the atman, your truest self, sometimes called the sakshi, the witness.

The verse adds that the wise, letting go of the idea that the senses are all there is, go beyond this world and become deathless. Here's where it lands. People usually identify with what's on the screen.
I'm angry. I'm tired. I'm this worry.
The Kena says the anger is a picture; you're closer to the light it's shown in. That doesn't make the anger fake, and it doesn't mean you shouldn't deal with it.

teach.h: A PLACE THE ANGER DOESN'T REACH.
teach.b: It means there's a place in you the anger doesn't reach.

teach.h: THE ATMAN IS THE EAR OF THE EAR.
teach.b: The atman, the ear of the ear, isn't hurt by a harsh word. It just hears it. Vedanta schools explain this light differently.
The Kena's point is that it's here: not far away, not somewhere you travel to, but behind every single thing you notice today.

how: In Vedanta teaching, Kena 1.2 ('the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind') is often used to point students toward awareness itself as distinct from what it perceives.

games.q: the student asked who makes the mind go. what does the teacher say?
o: 'it is the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind.'
games.why: the teacher points past each sense to what it runs on: the ear of the ear, the breath of breath.

practice: Close your eyes and listen to the sounds around you, a fan, traffic, your own breath, and let them come.
Then, instead of the sounds, notice the hearing itself, something aware that sound is happening, and rest there for a few breaths.
If a thought pulls you away, notice that something is aware of the thought too, and come back to the listening.

wordCard.voice: Shrotra, the ear, hearing. It is the ear of the ear, shrotrasya shrotram: something is aware of the hearing itself, the mind of the mind, the breath of breath.

orig.note: Sanskrit: shrotra, the ear, hearing; Kena 1.2: shrotrasya shrotram, the ear of the ear.
